COMPANY PLAN: H1 at 70% of the 22,000bn target means H2 needs only 6,520bn to hit it. The plan will almost certainly be beaten; it is not a useful benchmark.
actuals._MY_0853_INFERENCE_WAS_WRONG_2026_07_29: CORRECTION. At 08:53 today I inferred that VCBS's FY26 forecast of 18,055bn was TOTAL, hence 13,932 core, hence 23% below our bear branch - and concluded from three routes that the bear branch was 'not bearish enough'. The filing kills that inference. With H1 TOTAL already at 15,480, a full-year total of 18,055 would require H2 total of 2,575bn - about 1,288 a quarter, an 83% collapse. No broker forecasts that. So VCBS's 18,055 is almost certainly CORE, and on that reading it agrees with our bear branch of 18,061 to within 6bn. WHAT SURVIVES: the spread bridge's own spot-persists arithmetic, which was always the independent leg. WHAT DOES NOT: the claim that the street sits below our worst case. It does not. I over-read a single unlabelled broker number and built a three-route conclusion on it; two of those routes were the same route wearing different clothes.
actuals._US_REBAR_IS_TWO_DUTIES_NOT_ONE_2026_07_: MEASURE DISTINCTION on a tracked catalyst, and this file has been carrying only half of it. The watch list and calibration forecast #10 both describe 'US rebar AD/CVD final (prelim 121.97% on Hoa Phat)'. THE 121.97% IS THE ANTIDUMPING RATE ONLY. There are TWO separate investigations with two separate rates, and the COUNTERVAILING DUTY preliminary rate for Hoa Phat is 1.08% AD VALOREM, with 'All Others' also at 1.08% (Federal Register 2026-00495, published 13-Jan-2026, T1). So one of the two duties is already known to be trivial and only the AD side carries the headline number. Anything reading '122%' as the total burden is wrong by construction. THE TWO FINALS ARE ALIGNED - Commerce aligned the final CVD determination to issue on the SAME DATE as the final AD determination, so both land together or neither does. WHERE THE ~28-JUL DATE COMES FROM, which was never recorded here: HOA PHAT ITSELF REQUESTED THE POSTPONEMENT on 03-Mar-2026, with provisional measures extended for a period not to exceed six months. The January CVD notice had the final scheduled 'no later than 26-May-2026'; the March AD preliminary notice is titled 'Postponement of Final Determination and Extension of Provisional Measures'. The July date is the consequence of that request, not an arbitrary schedule. A company asking to delay a determination is ordinary procedure and is not read as a signal either way. CROSS-OWNED ENTITIES NAMED in the CVD determination: Hoa Phat Dung Quat Steel, Hoa Phat Hai Duong Steel, Hoa Phat Hung Yen Steel, Hoa Phat Energy. Relevant because the rate attaches to the group, not to one exporting entity. STATUS: STILL NOT PUBLISHED as of 20:54 ICT 29-Jul, one day past the expected date. Nothing changed in any branch. Calibration forecast #10 is unresolved, and this note sharpens what resolving it means: TWO rates must be read, not one.
actuals._US_REBAR_FINAL_ISSUED_2026_07_29: THE EVENT HAS RESOLVED, THE NUMBERS HAVE NOT. Commerce ISSUED THE FINAL DETERMINATIONS on 29-JUL-2026 covering rebar from Vietnam, Egypt and Bulgaria - one day after the date this repo had gated. Confirmed by legal trade press (Law360 headline 'US Finalizes Duties On Rebar From Vietnam, Egypt, Bulgaria'). Tier T5. THE FINAL RATES ARE NOT YET OBTAINABLE. federalregister.gov returns proxy 403 from here, and Vietnamese coverage as of 03:53 ICT 30-Jul still quotes only the PRELIMINARY figures - expected, since Commerce announced during US hours on 29-Jul and Vietnamese press will follow during the 30-Jul business day. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A PRELIMINARY OR PETITION FIGURE FOR THE FINAL. THE RATE STRUCTURE, NOW FULLY PINNED, all preliminary: ANTIDUMPING - Hoa Phat and affiliates 121.97% as the sole mandatory respondent, ALL OTHER Vietnamese exporters 130.77%. COUNTERVAILING - Hoa Phat 1.08%, All Others 1.08%. Affiliates named: Hoa Phat Hai Duong, Hoa Phat Dung Quat, Hoa Phat Hung Yen, Hoa Phat Energy. A LIVE CONFLATION TRAP, and press is already falling into it. Multiple outlets headline 'US imposes 130% tariff' or 'nearly 131%' WHILE NAMING HOA PHAT in the same sentence. 130.77% is the ALL-OTHERS rate. HOA PHAT'S RATE IS 121.97%, and it is lower precisely BECAUSE it was the mandatory respondent that participated. A separate petition figure of 117.61% also circulates and is neither the preliminary nor the final. FOUR NUMBERS ARE IN CIRCULATION FOR ONE CASE - 117.61 petition, 121.97 HPG preliminary, 130.77 all-others preliminary, and an unpublished final - and only one of them describes our holding. Same species as the AD-versus-CVD conflation logged 20:54 yesterday, one day later. WHAT THIS ALREADY TELLS US ABOUT FORECAST #10, registered now rather than after the rate lands. Provisional duties near 122% HAVE BEEN COLLECTED SINCE MARCH under the extension HPG itself requested. So HPG HAS ALREADY TRADED A FULL QUARTER UNDER THEM - and that quarter, Q2/2026 filed 29-Jul, printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. The commercial effect of losing US rebar is therefore ALREADY INSIDE THE REPORTED RUN-RATE rather than ahead of it. That is direct evidence for the forecast's stated reasoning - headline risk, not earnings risk - and it was available before the final. NOT SCORING YET: the forecast names the FINAL, and the final's numbers are not in hand. Recording the reasoning now means the eventual score cannot be constructed after the fact.
actuals._REVENUE_BLADE_IS_SPLITTING_2026_07_30: HPG RAISED DOMESTIC REBAR PRICES, and it qualifies my own 14:53 entry from yesterday. THE FACT: Hoa Phat Hung Yen raised high-grade rebar (CB400V, CB500V, B500B, Gr60) by 100 VND/kg ex-VAT in the North FROM 27-JUL. Reported as the FIFTH price adjustment of 2026, with several large mills raising from late July. Stated reason: input costs - iron ore, coking coal and SCRAP - staying high or trending up. Tier T5. WHAT IT QUALIFIES. The 29-Jul 14:53 entry read iron ore -5.3% m/m and coking coal -2.2% m/m as 'both cost blades easing, which is the one thing that would relieve HPG's H2 spread squeeze.' The Vietnamese trade view is the opposite: inputs anchored high or rising, which is WHY producers are raising prices. Both can be literally true - down slightly month-on-month, still high in level - but my framing was one-sided. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL: mills raising prices five times in seven months is not what an industry does when its input costs are easing. SCRAP IS A THIRD INPUT THIS FILE NEVER TRACKED. The spread bridge models ore and coking coal only. Vietnamese sources name scrap alongside them as a driver of the increases. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, AND THE BRIDGE CANNOT SEE IT: THE REVENUE BLADE IS SPLITTING. Domestic HRC prices were reported FALLING on 13-Jul under import competition, while REBAR prices are being RAISED. HRC down, rebar up, at the same time. hpg-spread-bridge.md section 5 already lists this as its first honest limit - 'Product mix is ignored - HPG sells rebar as well as HRC, with different economics' - and that limit is now BINDING rather than theoretical. A bridge calibrated on a single HRC blade cannot represent a quarter where the two products move in opposite directions. NOTHING CHANGED. No branch, probability or weight. This is T5 and charter s2 forbids moving probs or exit_pe on T4-T6. It is recorded because H2 spread is the live variable on 16.8% of the book and because the direction of the revenue blade is now genuinely ambiguous rather than simply negative. Corroborating levels, both already consistent with this file: domestic HRC 14,000-14,350 VND/kg; iron ore ~98.02 USD/dmtu on 08-Jul against the 98.25 logged yesterday.
actuals._US_REBAR_FINAL_RATES_2026_07_30: THE FINAL RATES ARE PUBLISHED. Federal Register 2026-15438 (AD, Final Affirmative Determination of Sales at Less Than Fair Value) and 2026-15437 (CVD, Final Affirmative Countervailing Duty Determination), both dated 30-JUL-2026, applicable 30-Jul. Period of investigation 01-Oct-2024 to 31-Mar-2025. Tier T1 for the existence and dates; the RATES below are T5, from trade press, because federalregister.gov returns proxy 403 from this environment and the documents themselves could not be read. THE NUMBERS: FINAL DUMPING MARGINS FOR VIETNAM 128.53% TO 136.57%, with CASH DEPOSIT RATES ADJUSTED TO 123.49% TO 131.53% after offsetting export subsidies. Preliminary was 121.97% (Hoa Phat, mandatory respondent) to 130.77% (all others). SO THE FINALS CAME IN ABOUT 6.6pp HIGHER AT BOTH ENDS. WHICH END IS HOA PHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED, AND I AM NOT ASSERTING IT. The preliminary structure put the mandatory respondent at the LOWER rate, so 128.53% is the likely Hoa Phat figure and 136.57% the all-others - but that is an inference from structure, not a reading of the table. This is precisely the conflation warned about in _US_REBAR_IS_TWO_DUTIES_NOT_ONE_2026_07_29, and the warning applies to my own inference as much as to the press. USEFUL MECHANIC WORTH RECORDING: the CASH DEPOSIT RATE IS ~5pp BELOW THE MARGIN because of an export-subsidy offset between the AD and CVD cases. The deposit is what importers actually post, so it is the operative number for trade economics, not the headline margin. WHAT IT DOES TO THE THESIS: NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March under the extension HPG itself requested. HPG has already traded a full quarter under them, and that quarter - Q2/2026, filed 29-Jul - printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51%. Moving a prohibitive duty from ~122% to ~129% changes nothing commercially: the trade was already uneconomic and the earnings effect is already inside the reported run-rate. US is ~3% of revenue. No branch, probability, weight or confidence changed.
actuals._REBAR_IS_NOT_OVER_2026_07_31: CORRECTION TO A STATUS I RECORDED YESTERDAY. The date-gate row was marked 'RESOLVED 30-Jul' after Commerce published its final AD and CVD determinations. COMMERCE'S PART IS RESOLVED. THE CASE IS NOT. WHAT REMAINS: the US INTERNATIONAL TRADE COMMISSION must make its FINAL INJURY DETERMINATION WITHIN 45 DAYS of Commerce's finals, so a vote around MID-SEPTEMBER 2026. ONLY AFTER AN AFFIRMATIVE ITC VOTE DO THE ORDERS ACTUALLY ISSUE. If the ITC finds no material injury, no duties are imposed at all and cash deposits collected under the provisional measures are REFUNDED. WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN FILING AWAY: THE REMAINING UNCERTAINTY ON REBAR IS NOW ASYMMETRIC TO THE UPSIDE, and nothing in this file models it. The DOWNSIDE - duties imposed at ~129% - is already inside the reported run-rate, because provisional duties near 122% have been collected since March and HPG's Q2 printed revenue +53% and NPAT +51% under them. The UPSIDE - an ITC negative, orders never issuing, deposits refunded - is not in any branch. ITC negatives in steel cases are uncommon but they are not unheard of, and the petition covers four countries so a split outcome by country is possible. NOT ADDING A BRANCH OR MOVING A PROBABILITY - both are judgment changes reserved for a human under charter s2. Recorded as a DATED CATALYST that belongs on the calendar, which is charter s1 test 3. FORECAST #10'S SCORE IS UNAFFECTED. It named the Commerce final explicitly ('~Jul 28 Federal Register') and that is what resolved it. The ITC vote is a separate event and does not reopen a scored forecast.
actuals._A_THIRD_FIGURE_FOR_THE_DIVESTMENT_GAIN_: OPEN-DECISIONS ITEM 13 MOVED FURTHER FROM RESOLUTION, NOT CLOSER, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. A THIRD CANDIDATE FIGURE APPEARED THIS SWEEP: press states that in Q1/2026 APPROXIMATELY 3,800bn came from the capital-transfer at the PHO NOI urban project. Tier T5, and explicitly approximate ('khoang'). THERE ARE NOW THREE NUMBERS FOR ONE LINE: 4,123 as carried in q1_divestment_gain; 4,010 as implied by q1_npat 9,056 minus q1_core_npat 5,046; and ~3,800 from this sweep. 3,800 is 7.8% below the file's figure and 5.2% below the implied one - TOO FAR TO BE A ROUNDING OF EITHER. IT WEAKENS THE EXPLANATION THIS FILE PREFERRED. The existing note offers 'likely explanation: 4,123 is PRE-tax and 4,010 is post-tax, implying 113bn of tax = a 2.7% effective rate, well below the 20% CIT - possible but not obvious'. A COMPETING READING NOW HAS SUPPORT: that ~3,800 IS PHO NOI ALONE while 4,123 is TOTAL divestment or other income including roughly 300bn of something else. On that reading the 113bn gap is COMPOSITION, not tax, and the tax story is unnecessary. THE FILE'S OWN H1 NON-STEEL RECONCILIATION assumed the whole 4,123 was Pho Noi ('Pho Noi one-off 4,123 + agriculture ~648 = 4,771'), so that reconciliation inherits the same ambiguity. NEITHER READING IS ESTABLISHED AND NEITHER IS ADOPTED. WHAT IT COSTS, QUANTIFIED. q1_core_npat / q1_volume_mt is the CALIBRATION ANCHOR of the spread bridge - conversion_usd_t 114 was solved backwards to reproduce it. The three candidates give: gain 4,123 -> core 4,933 -> anchor 1.644m/t; gain 4,010 -> core 5,046 -> anchor 1.682m/t; gain 3,800 -> core 5,256 -> anchor 1.752m/t. THE ANCHOR RANGE IS 1.644 TO 1.752m/t, A 6.5% SPREAD, and the new figure moves it in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION from the alternative previously considered - the file had only ever contemplated the anchor being LOWER than 1.68, and 3,800 makes it HIGHER. The bridge's whole cost structure is calibrated off this one number. A CHECK THAT DOES PASS, recorded so it is not re-litigated: 4,123 is a Q1 figure, not an H1 one. Q1 9,056 + Q2 6,424 = 15,480 = stated H1 exactly, so the quarters are clean and the gain sits inside Q1. NOTHING CHANGED. q1_divestment_gain is NOT edited - three candidate values is a reason to escalate, not to pick. The resolving document is HPG's Q1 or H1 financial statement note on other income, which this environment cannot reach.
actuals._HPG_HAD_NO_BALANCE_SHEET_AND_THERE_IS_A: HPG'S BLOCK CONTAINED NOTHING ON DEBT, BORROWINGS, CAPEX, CASH FLOW OR INVENTORY - ZERO HITS ON ALL FIVE. That is 16.8% of the book with a proposed ADD of +3.2pp, mid-way through DUNG QUAT 2, one of the largest industrial capex programmes in Vietnam. COMPARE KDH, WHOSE BLOCK CARRIES BORROWINGS, INVENTORY, OPERATING CASH FLOW AND D/E. THE DEVELOPER GOT A BALANCE SHEET; THE CAPEX-HEAVY STEELMAKER DID NOT. AND THE WHOLE WEEKEND WENT INTO HPG'S SPREAD - ore, coal, HRC, the bridge, the calibration anchor - WHICH IS A PURE P&L EXERCISE. A capex-heavy cyclical's risk is at least as much balance sheet as margin. NOW ON FILE: BORROWINGS OF MORE THAN 90,617bn AT END-Q1/2026. CONSTRUCTION IN PROGRESS ROSE SHARPLY TO OVER 10,328bn AND Q1 INVESTING CASH FLOW WAS MINUS 2,921bn. One outlet frames it as Hoa Phat 'straining to balance profit, cash flow and enormous debt pressure'. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS AN ACCOUNTING INFLECTION THE BRIDGE CANNOT SEE. Sources state that ONCE DUNG QUAT 2 REACHES FULL CAPACITY, HOA PHAT NO LONGER CAPITALISES INTEREST INTO CONSTRUCTION IN PROGRESS, SO ALL INTEREST EXPENSE FLOWS STRAIGHT INTO THE INCOME STATEMENT. THE SPREAD BRIDGE MODELS ORE, COAL, HRC AND A CONVERSION COST. IT DOES NOT MODEL INTEREST AT ALL. So a step-change in reported earnings can arrive with the spread completely unchanged, and nothing in this file would anticipate it. SCALE, WITH THE UNKNOWN NAMED. At 90,617bn of borrowings a blended 5-7% implies 4,531-6,343bn of annual interest, which is 19-27% OF THE CORE BASE BRANCH OF 23,336bn. WHAT SHARE WAS BEING CAPITALISED IS UNKNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED - the impact is the newly-expensed portion, not the whole. The range is recorded to show the order of magnitude of the line the model omits, NOT as an estimate of the hit. THIS IS THE KDH LESSON'S MIRROR. At KDH a ONE-OFF GAIN masked a core collapse and made reported profit look better than the business. At HPG a CAPITALISED COST BECOMING AN EXPENSED ONE would make reported profit look worse than the business. BOTH ARE PRESENTATION EFFECTS THAT THE OPERATING MODEL CANNOT SEE, and this file has now been caught by the first one. TWO TRAPS HANDLED. (1) ENTITY: the same coverage gives 'total assets 5,239.3bn' and 'inventory +23.5% to 546.8bn' - the source itself labels these CONG TY PHAT TRIEN NONG NGHIEP HOA PHAT, THE AGRICULTURE SUBSIDIARY, NOT HPG. HPG's total assets are two orders of magnitude larger. NOT LOGGED AS HPG. (2) VINTAGE: a separate item gives 'borrowings over 65,000bn with idle cash near 35,000bn'. That is a DIFFERENT AND OLDER VINTAGE than the 90,617bn, so THE TWO ARE NOT MERGED AND NO NET DEBT IS COMPUTED ACROSS THEM. ESCALATED, NOT MODELLED - adding an interest line to the bridge is a rebuild and human-only under charter s4.
actuals._CAP_NOW_CROSS_CHECK_2026_08_02_1153: CAP_NOW IS 7.6% TOO LOW - mu_raw +15.1% -> +6.4%, a 8.8pp move. actuals._THE_MISSING_INTEREST_LINE_IS_NOW_SIZED_: THE SPREAD BRIDGE'S MISSING INTEREST LINE HAS BEEN FLAGGED TWICE WITHOUT A NUMBER. IT NOW HAS ONE, AND IT IS BIG. HPG'S FINANCIAL DEBT REACHED A RECORD 98,530bn AT 30-JUN-2026, UP 9% FROM END-2025, driven mainly by SHORT-TERM borrowing for working capital. Q1/2026 financial costs roughly DOUBLED to ~1,868bn, of which INTEREST EXPENSE WAS OVER 1,333bn - about 15bn PER DAY (1,333/90 = 14.8, which checks). SIZED AGAINST THE THING THE WHOLE MODEL TURNS ON. Q1 volume is 3.0m tonnes (H1 6.5 minus Q2 3.5), so INTEREST IS ~444,000 DONG PER TONNE = 0.444m/t. The bridge's core NPAT/tonne branches are bear 1.25, base 1.60, bull 1.85, with Q1 actual core at 1.68. SO INTEREST RUNS AT 24% OF THE BULL BRANCH, 28% OF BASE AND 35.5% OF BEAR. Annualised at the Q1 run-rate it is 5,332bn, or 24.2% of the 22,000bn FY profit target. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN - THE DISTINCTION MATTERS. NPAT is struck AFTER interest, so interest is already INSIDE the observed core NPAT/tonne; this does not mean the model double-counts or omits it arithmetically. WHAT IT MEANS IS THAT THE BRIDGE HAS NO LINE THAT RESPONDS TO IT. Volume and spread move across the three branches; interest per tonne is held constant by construction. With debt UP 9% in six months and financial costs DOUBLING year on year, holding it constant is an assumption that the evidence now contradicts - and it bites hardest in the bear branch, where it is over a third of the whole figure. IT ALSO COMPOUNDS WITH THE USD/VND FINDING. The dong's central rate hit a record 25,338 on 1-Aug. IF any material share of this debt is USD-denominated, a depreciating dong raises the domestic-currency cost of servicing it on top of the volume increase. THE CURRENCY MIX OF HPG'S DEBT IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT ASSUMED - it is the next cheap check, and it is one line off the filed balance sheet. A FIGURE REJECTED IN THE SAME SOURCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-ADOPTED. The summary carrying the debt number also stated H1 after-tax profit of 'over 10,539bn, completing 67% of the annual plan'. THAT IS NOT THIS YEAR. The file's 15,480bn is corroborated THREE WAYS: it is 70.4% of the 22,000bn target as reported; Q1 9,056 + Q2 6,424 = 15,480 EXACTLY; and 15,480 against H1/2025's 7,600 is +104%, matching the filed +103%. 10,539 at 67% implies a plan near 15,730bn, which is a 2025-vintage plan (FY2025 actual was 15,515bn). The revenue figure in the same summary - 108,870bn, +47% - IS the correct H1/2026 one, so the source mixes a current revenue with a prior-year profit. SECOND TIME IN TWO HOURS THAT A SUMMARY HAS BUNDLED A TRUE CURRENT FACT WITH A STALE ONE. NOTHING MODELLED - branch construction is human-only under charter section 4. Confidence NOT moved: no input changed, and this argues for re-deriving the branches rather than scaling them.

actuals._THE_INTEREST_STEP_IS_STRUCTURAL_NOT_CYC: RAN THE CURRENCY-MIX CHECK NAMED AT 02:53. IT DID NOT ANSWER THAT QUESTION - recorded as still open - BUT IT RETURNED THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE INTEREST STEP, WHICH IS WORTH MORE. THE MECHANISM: AFTER DUNG QUAT 2 REACHED FULL CAPACITY, HOA PHAT NO LONGER CAPITALISES BORROWING COSTS INTO CONSTRUCTION-IN-PROGRESS AS IT DID BEFORE. While DQ2 was being built, interest on the debt funding it was capitalised into the asset and never touched the income statement. Now it is EXPENSED. THAT IS WHY Q1/2026 INTEREST IS DOUBLE THE SAME PERIOD OF 2024 AND 14% ABOVE Q4/2025. THIS IS A STRUCTURAL, PERMANENT, ONE-DIRECTION CHANGE IN THE P&L - NOT A CYCLICAL SWING - AND THE 14% QUARTER-ON-QUARTER STEP SAYS IT IS STILL WORKING THROUGH. THE DEBT PATH, AND ALMOST ALL OF IT IS Q2. Total borrowings and finance leases were ~90,600bn at end-MAR (about 69% SHORT-TERM, ~62,800bn) against 98,530bn at end-JUN. Implied end-2025 is ~90,394bn from the +9% YTD already on file. SO DEBT WAS ESSENTIALLY FLAT IN Q1 (+206bn) AND ROSE 7,930bn IN Q2 (+8.8%). The borrowing is recent and short-dated. AND HERE IS THE PART THAT CHANGES HOW THE BRIDGE SHOULD BE READ. INTEREST PER TONNE IS INVERSELY GEARED TO VOLUME, SO IT PUNISHES THE BEAR BRANCH SPECIFICALLY. At a full-year interest run-rate near 5,682bn (Q1 actual plus three quarters at the debt-adjusted Q2 rate of ~1,450bn): bear FY volume 13.5m t gives 0.421m/t = 33.7% of a 1.25m core NPAT/tonne; base 14.5m t gives 0.392m/t = 24.5% of 1.60m; bull 15.5m t gives 0.367m/t = 19.8% of 1.85m. THE BEAR CASE IS HIT TWICE - LOW VOLUME AND, BECAUSE OF THAT SAME LOW VOLUME, THE HIGHEST INTEREST BURDEN PER TONNE. Yesterday's 02:53 note established that no branch RESPONDS to interest; this establishes that the direction it would respond in is ADVERSE TO THE DOWNSIDE, which is the branch a risk model exists to get right. STATED FAIRLY, THE OTHER SIDE: interest per tonne FALLS as DQ2 volume ramps - 0.421 to 0.367 across the branches - WHICH IS PRECISELY THE POINT OF THE INVESTMENT. This is not a story about a broken balance sheet; it is operating leverage working in both directions, and the model currently shows neither. THE CURRENCY QUESTION IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT GUESSED. Two searches failed to establish the currency mix of the debt. WHAT IS BOUNDED: Q1 financial costs of 1,868bn less interest of 1,333bn leaves 535bn OF NON-INTEREST FINANCIAL COST. For a company importing iron ore and coking coal in USD with a record-high dong, FX is the obvious candidate - AND IT IS ONLY A CANDIDATE. 535bn is an upper bound on any FX loss in the quarter, not a measurement of one. STILL THE NEXT CHEAP CHECK, still one line off the filed statement. NOTHING MODELLED; branch construction is human-only. Confidence NOT moved - this sharpens OPEN-DECISIONS item 28 rather than changing an input.
actuals._WHICH_END_IS_HOA_PHAT_ANSWERED_AND_IT_D: THE LAST OPEN CELL IN THE REBAR CASE CLOSES. us_rebar_ad_final_range_pct has held [128.53, 136.57] since 30-Jul with this file's own note: 'THE FINALS CAME IN ABOUT 6.6pp HIGHER AT BOTH ENDS. WHICH END IS HOA PHAT IS NOT CONFIRMED, AND I AM NOT ASSERTING IT.' The range was known; the assignment was not. ANSWER: THE HOA PHAT GROUP COMPANIES CARRY 128.53% - the LOW end - and the Vietnam-wide entity carries 136.57%. IT RECONCILES TO THE STRUCTURE ALREADY ON FILE, WHICH IS THE REASON TO BELIEVE IT: the preliminary had Hoa Phat at 121.97% as sole mandatory respondent against 130.77% all-others, a gap of 8.80pp; the final preserves the ordering and nearly the gap at 8.04pp, with Hoa Phat +6.56pp and all-others +5.80pp. And the export-subsidy offset implied by us_rebar_cash_deposit_range_pct is 5.04pp AT BOTH ENDS (128.53-123.49 = 136.57-131.53 = 5.04), so HPG'S CASH DEPOSIT RATE IS 123.49%. AND THE FINDING IS THAT IT CHANGES NOTHING. This file has tracked which rate applies to HPG since 29-Jul across three entries on the implicit premise that the distinction mattered. AT 128.53% VERSUS 136.57%, BOTH RATES ARE PROHIBITIVE. Being 8.04pp better than an exporter who is also shut out of the market is worth nothing. The only outcome that would have mattered is a rate low enough to keep shipping and neither end is that. The relative-advantage read - 'HPG got the better rate because it participated' - is true and economically void. NO MODEL EFFECT: rebar into the US is ~3% of HPG revenue and the brief carries it as headline risk only, a Layer-4 flag, not a model input. CONFIDENCE UNMOVED per charter s2 - this is trade press reporting a Federal Register determination, NOT the determination, the same tier that has governed every rebar entry in this case. federalregister.gov and trade.gov both returned proxy 403 again this hour. Forecast #10 was already scored HIT on 29-Jul and is NOT re-scored; what closed today is a sub-question, not the forecast. NO ESCALATION TRIGGER FIRES.
actuals._CORE_GATE_DERIVED_AND_GIVEN_A_STATUTORY: THE DATE IS NOW DERIVED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST, AND THE DERIVATION EXPLAINS IT. The gate row carries 'PRELIMINARY DETERMINATION intended 24-AUG-2026' from press. 19 CFR 351.226 sets the preliminary at 150 DAYS from publication of the initiation notice. Initiation published 25-Mar-2026; +150 days = SATURDAY 22-AUG-2026, WHICH ROLLS TO MONDAY 24-AUG. The file's date is right, and right for a reason nothing in the file recorded - a future sweep computing 150 days and getting 22-Aug would otherwise have 'found' an error that is not one. THE OUTER BOUND, WHICH THE FILE DID NOT HAVE. The gate row's caveat reads 'extensions are routine - treat 24-Aug as an intention' - true but UNBOUNDED. The same regulation sets the FINAL at 300 DAYS, and if the Secretary concludes the inquiry is extraordinarily complicated may extend that by NO MORE THAN 65 DAYS. So: FINAL 19-JAN-2027; STATUTORY MAXIMUM 25-MAR-2027. THIS GATE CAN SLIP SEVEN MONTHS AND STILL BE LAWFUL. Treating 24-Aug as decisive would be a mistake and the size of that mistake is now bounded. Same species as the 27-Oct-2026 outer bound placed on Decision 612: an intention plus a statutory ceiling is a usable gate, an intention alone is not.
actuals._A_THIRD_CORE_CIRCUMVENTION_INQUIRY_NAME: The file holds two March documents - FR 2026-05808 (Vietnam CORE orders; CORE finished in INDONESIA from VIETNAMESE cold-rolled steel) and FR 2026-05807 (Chinese substrate via Indonesia). A THIRD EXISTS AND THIS FILE DOES NOT HOLD IT: FR 2026-13607, published 06-JUL-2026, 'Certain Corrosion-Resistant Steel Products From the People's Republic of China: Initiation of Circumvention Inquiry on the Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Orders'. Different document, different month, different underlying orders. Its 150-day preliminary would fall 03-DEC-2026. ITS SCOPE IS NOT KNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED. Only the title and date are in hand. WHY IT IS LOGGED UNRESOLVED: an inquiry into circumvention of the CHINA CORE orders turns on WHICH THIRD COUNTRY DOES THE FINISHING, and Vietnam is historically the principal route for Chinese CORE. IF Vietnam is a named third country, the exposure runs the OPPOSITE WAY from the March case - Vietnamese finishing of Chinese substrate, not Vietnamese substrate finished abroad - which would be a DIRECT Vietnamese-producer exposure rather than a second-order one. THIS IS A POSSIBILITY, NOT A FINDING. Field that would retire it: the third-country scope named in FR 2026-13607. federalregister.gov is gateway-blocked, so this needs press or an unblocked mirror. NO CHANGE TO HPG'S POSITION: rebar into the US is ~3% of revenue, the March Vietnam inquiry is country-wide with no Vietnamese producer named, and HPG makes HRC - the substrate for cold-rollers - not CRS itself.
actuals._THE_THIRD_INQUIRY_IS_THAILAND_NOT_VIETN: THE OPEN ITEM CREATED AT 03:53 IS CLOSED, AND IT CLOSES AGAINST THE INFERENCE I DECLINED TO MAKE. FR 2026-13607 covers CORE FROM CHINA COMPLETED IN THAILAND USING CHINESE COMPONENTS, filed by Nucor and Steel Dynamics, initiated 06-Jul-2026. VIETNAM IS NOT INVOLVED. WHY THE 03:53 ENTRY WAS WRITTEN AS IT WAS: it logged that 'Vietnam is historically the principal route for Chinese CORE... IF Vietnam is a named third country, the exposure runs the OPPOSITE way from the March case... This is a possibility, not a finding.' THE HISTORICAL BASE RATE POINTED AT VIETNAM AND THE ANSWER IS THAILAND. Had it been asserted, this file would have published a false DIRECT trade exposure on a 16.8% position and be withdrawing it now - the fourth withdrawal of the week. Named at 03:53 with the resolving field stated, closed at 04:53, NO CORRECTION REQUIRED. THE MAP IS NOW COMPLETE - THREE INQUIRIES, ONE TOUCHES VIETNAM. FR 2026-05808 (25-Mar): Vietnam CORE orders, CORE finished in INDONESIA from VIETNAMESE cold-rolled steel; preliminary 24-Aug-2026, final 19-Jan-2027, statutory ceiling 25-Mar-2027. FR 2026-05807 (25-Mar): Chinese substrate via Indonesia. FR 2026-13607 (06-Jul): China CORE orders, finished in THAILAND from Chinese components; preliminary ~03-Dec-2026, Vietnam absent. ONLY THE FIRST TOUCHES VIETNAM, AND AS THE SUBSTRATE ORIGIN RATHER THAN THE FINISHER - and HPG makes HRC, not CRS, so even that one is second-order. No change to HPG's position on any of the three. A PATTERN NAMED AND A FORWARD INFERENCE DECLINED: Nucor and Steel Dynamics are the requesters on all three and all three attack THIRD-COUNTRY ROUTING - Indonesia-from-Vietnam, Indonesia-from-China, Thailand-from-China. That is a campaign, not three coincidences, and it is a fact. Whether it implies a future Vietnam-as-finisher case is SPECULATION ABOUT FILINGS THAT DO NOT EXIST and is NOT logged as risk.
actuals._FIRST_CRITERION_ACTUALLY_TESTED_THIS_WE: 'Core NPAT/tonne < VND1.25m for two consecutive quarters.' THE FILE'S OWN CONVENTION REPRODUCES EXACTLY: q1_core_npat 5,046 over (h1_volume_mt 6.5 - q2_volume_mt 3.5 = 3.0mt) = VND 1.682m/t, matching the file's stated Q1 core of 1.682m/t to three decimals - so the convention is core NPAT divided by TOTAL steel volume, and it is now documented. Q2: core 11,357 - 5,046 = VND 6,311bn over 3.5mt = VND 1.803m/t. BOTH QUARTERS ARE 35% AND 44% ABOVE THE THRESHOLD. NOT MET, AND NOT CLOSE. THIS IS THE FIRST OF THE SEVENTEEN RUN TO A VERDICT RATHER THAN FOUND BROKEN, and it matters that the verdict is a PASS: seven consecutive defect findings make it easy to assume the whole set is rotten. It is not; 29% of it works.
actuals._DQ2_NAMEPLATE_ESTABLISHED_AND_THE_CRITE: WENT TO CLOSE ONE OF THE FOUR CONDITIONAL CRITERIA AND IT GOT WORSE, NOT BETTER. THE NUMBER, AND IT IS SOLID: DUNG QUAT 2's DESIGN CAPACITY IS 5.6 MILLION TONNES OF HRC PER YEAR - stated consistently across trade press and HPG's own subsidiary site, alongside a separately-approved +500,000t expansion. The 07:53 audit listed 'HRC volume run-rate < 85% of nameplate at Q4' as CONDITIONAL because 'nameplate is not on file'. It is on file now. AND THAT IS WHEN THE REAL DEFECT SHOWS. The condition is 'DQ2 ramp disappoints' - IT NAMES DQ2. But the disclosed figure is GROUP HRC VOLUME (q2_hrc_volume_mt = 1.9), not DQ2's. THE CRITERION ASKS ABOUT ONE PLANT AND THE DATA MEASURES THE WHOLE COMPANY. THE TWO DENOMINATORS GIVE INCOMPARABLE ANSWERS. Q2 HRC 1.9mt annualises to 7.6mt. Against DQ2's 5.6mt: 135.7%, meaningless because group volume includes DQ1's output. Against total HRC of ~9mt: 84.4%, FRACTIONALLY BELOW THE 85% THRESHOLD. THE ~9mt IS SOFT AND IS LABELLED SOFT: the source says 'HRC AND HIGH-QUALITY STEEL capacity reaching approximately 9 million tonnes' - broader than HRC alone - and DQ1's own HRC line is not established here (~3.4mt only by subtraction, which is inference). THE SOLID NUMBER IS DQ2'S 5.6mt; THE ONE THE DATA WOULD NEED IS THE SOFT ONE. AUDIT REVISED, AND THE REVISION IS A DOWNGRADE: this criterion moves CONDITIONAL -> NOT TESTABLE for a DIFFERENT reason than before - not missing data but a SUBJECT/MEASURE MISMATCH, the third instance of that species after MBB's MBV drag and VCI's foreign-versus-total brokerage share. NEW TALLY: 5 TESTABLE, 9 NOT TESTABLE, 3 CONDITIONAL - not-testable is now 53%, a majority, where the 07:53 audit had 47%. ONE THING FOR THE HUMAN REGARDLESS OF WORDING: on the group-HRC reading the run-rate already sits essentially ON the threshold at 84.4%. That is a Q2 figure against a Q4 test, in a plant still ramping (DQ2's second blast furnace first cast Sept-2025), so the run-rate should RISE into Q4 and this is NOT a warning. What it means is that the Q4 TEST IS LIVE RATHER THAN ACADEMIC: the denominator choice will decide the answer, and the denominator is undefined. NOTHING MODELLED, NO CRITERION STATUS CHANGED, NO CONFIDENCE MOVED.
actuals._THE_STEEL_PEERS_TEST_THE_SPREAD_FROM_OU: THE GAP FIRST: 'NKG', 'Nam Kim', 'Hoa Sen' and 'HSG' returned exactly ONE hit in assumptions.json before this entry - a passing note that they sit in the coated-steel product line under a MoIT decision. NO RESULTS, NO MARGINS, on the two listed companies that BUY WHAT HPG MAKES. Lane 6 exists to catch peers that reprice our names and had never been run on the steel side. THE Q2 PRINTS. NKG: NPAT VND 102.6bn against a small loss a year earlier; GROSS MARGIN 7.1% -> 10.5%, +3.40pp; H1 revenue VND 7,411.6bn (-6.2%), H1 NPAT VND 124.1bn (+98.1%). HSG: NPAT ~VND 382.3bn (+39.6%); revenue VND 10,267bn (+5.2%) with gross profit VND 1,526bn (+25.8%), a GROSS MARGIN OF 14.86% AGAINST AN IMPLIED 12.43% a year earlier - +2.43pp; H1 NPAT VND 568bn (-12%) on a high base. HPG: core NPAT/tonne 1.682m -> 1.803m, +7.2%, derived 07:53 from this file's own convention. THE POINT IS WHAT THIS RULES OUT. NKG and HSG BUY HRC; HPG SELLS it. IF HPG'S Q2 SPREAD GAIN HAD COME FROM RAISING PRICES INTO ITS OWN CUSTOMERS, THEIR GROSS MARGINS WOULD HAVE COMPRESSED. BOTH EXPANDED - by 3.40pp and 2.43pp. So the improvement is CHAIN-WIDE, NOT ZERO-SUM, and HPG's gain was not taken out of the downstream. THAT POINTS AT THE RAW-MATERIAL END, AND THIS FILE ALREADY HAS THAT LEG: coking coal at US$228 FOB Australia, down an eighth consecutive week, and iron ore roughly flat at ~93.66 (62% Fe CFR Tianjin). A falling input cost widens the whole chain at once, which is the pattern observed. THE LIMIT, STATED: THE MECHANISM IS INFERRED; THE SIMULTANEITY IS ESTABLISHED. Three companies' margins moving the same way in one quarter is not a cost decomposition. What the data supports is the NEGATIVE claim - the zero-sum explanation is excluded - and that is worth more here, because the zero-sum reading is the one that would have argued HPG's Q2 was borrowed from its customers and reversible. WHERE THE STREET WAS: VCBS forecast HPG's Q2 profit growth at +25%, with HSG and NKG 'hut hoi' (running out of breath). HPG'S ACTUAL WAS +50.9% (6,424 against 4,256.75), 2.04x THE FORECAST GROWTH RATE, and both peers GREW rather than lagged. Context on street positioning, NOT a scored forecast - it is not this file's prediction. BEARING ON THE BRANCHES: this does NOT move core_npat_per_tonne_m (bear 1.25 / base 1.6 / bull 1.85), a charter s4 judgement input, untouched. But the bear branch requires the spread to break, and the quarter in which it would have had to start breaking is one in which HPG's CUSTOMERS GOT MORE PROFITABLE, not less. The armed criterion was tested and passed at 07:53; this is a second, independent line pointing the same way. NOTHING MODELLED, NO CONFIDENCE MOVED - T5 press on filed peer statements, and peers are not this book.

spread_bridge_2026_07_26._COKING_COAL_CORRECTED_2026_07_28: CORRECTION, and it REVERSES the direction of the 27-Jul conclusion. THE ERROR: _BOTH_INPUTS_VERIFIED_2026_07_27 states 'Coking coal SPOT 228 (PHCC FOB Australia, -24% MoM from 238.9 on 10-Jul)'. Those two clauses contradict each other on their own figures - 238.9 to 228 is -4.6%, not -24%. spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28: The bridge carries FX 26,300 described only as 'VND/USD market rate'. On 28-Jul there are two very different market rates: the SBV CENTRAL rate at 25,306 - an all-time high, passing the 25,298 set 25-Aug-2025 - and the FREE MARKET at 26,400-26,420. A 4.4% gap. The 26,300 in file sits 0.4% below the free market and 3.9% above the central rate, so it appears to be a free-market figure, but nothing says so. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS DEPENDS ON SOMETHING THE BRIDGE ALSO DOES NOT STATE: whether HPG's realised HRC price is treated as USD-linked or VND-fixed. If USD-LINKED, FX multiplies a USD margin of (539 - 522) and largely CANCELS - the choice between the two rates is worth about VND 0.019m/t, trivial. If VND-FIXED, FX hits only the USD cost side and the choice is worth VND 0.576m/t - 85 to 96% of the 0.60-0.68m/t spot margin and 46% of the 1.25m bear branch. REALITY IS IN BETWEEN: roughly 80% of HRC volume is domestic and priced in VND, tracking import parity with a lag and imperfectly - and the Formosa price cut suggests domestic prices are currently set by competition rather than by FX. So partial pass-through. But the bridge does not say, which means it cannot be interrogated on the question, and that is the defect. NOT CHANGED. No branch moves and nothing here is an escalation. spread_bridge_2026_07_26._FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29: ANSWERS the open question in _FX_IS_UNLABELLED_2026_07_28, which asked which of several 'market rates' applies to HPG's imports. spread_bridge_2026_07_26._ANCHOR_IS_CONTAMINATED_BY_NON_STEEL_202: THIRD problem found with the 1.682m/t calibration anchor, and this one has a clear direction. Hoa Phat AGRICULTURE (HPA) filed H1/2026 today: revenue 3,379bn, NPAT 648bn, 64% of its full-year plan, implying an FY plan near 1,012bn. HPG Group itself is still unfiled. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: this bridge models HPG as a STEEL business - NPAT per tonne times tonnes - and its conversion_usd_t of 114 was SOLVED BACKWARDS so the bridge reproduces a Q1 core anchor of 1.682m/t (5,046bn over 3.0mt). But that 5,046bn is GROUP profit and includes non-steel earnings. SIZING WITH AGRICULTURE ALONE: HPA runs about 324bn a quarter, so (5,046 - 324) / 3.0mt = 1.574m/t - 6.4% below the anchor. And agriculture is only one non-steel segment; real estate, appliances, pipe and galvanised sheet also sit outside the 3.0mt basket, so a true steel-only margin is lower still. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: an anchor that is too HIGH means the solved conversion cost is too LOW, so the bridge UNDERSTATES steel costs and OVERSTATES the spread at every price point. That is the same direction as the other two anchor problems - the 113bn core/one-off reconciliation gap (_RECONCILIATION_FLAG_2026_07_28) and the FX rate sitting 0.87% below the bank sell rate (_FX_RATE_PINNED_2026_07_29). Three separate issues, all pushing the modelled spread the same way: too generous. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: HPA's ownership percentage, so how much of the 648bn is attributable to HPG shareholders is unknown; and whether HPA's profit is inside the 5,046bn 'core' figure at all, which depends on how that core number was constructed. Both read off the segment note in the group statement. NOT APPLIED. Re-solving the conversion cost on an inferred non-steel share would replace one unverified anchor with another. The group statement lands within a day and carries the segment note that settles it.

The 15:53 entry named the possibility and refused to infer it; the refusal is now discharged with a number rather than left hanging. A minority sell-down inside a consolidated subsidiary raises consolidated equity and creates a 15% NCI. IT DOES NOT CREATE A P&L GAIN.

A HYPOTHESIS I FORMED AND THEN KILLED. Reading 'dinh gia cao nhat nganh' - the highest valuation in its sector - I expected HPA to have been floated at a PREMIUM multiple to its parent, which would have been a governance point. SECOND CAVEAT, CARRIED FORWARD RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED: the coal 212 is BASIS-DISCLAIMED BY ITS OWN PUBLISHER ('a broader coking coal price rather than specifically PHCC FOB Australia'), logged at 08:53 as a CANDIDATE falsification, not a settled one. If coal is left at 220 the implied figure is VND1.042m and the gap to bear is -16.6%, not -7.7%. BOTH READINGS ARE GIVEN. THIRD: the ore print is T4 - tradingeconomics.com is egress-blocked and this was read through a search summary. NOTHING MODELLED. core_npat_per_tonne_m (bear 1.25 / base 1.6 / bull 1.85) IS UNTOUCHED - charter section 4 human-only. NO CONFIDENCE MOVED. NO TRIGGER FIRES: this does not move a computed E[r] because no model input was changed; it sizes the distance between the bridge and the branches, which is a human's call to act on.

actuals._target_conflict: Now corroborated at 30-35%, matching dossiers/MBB.md. Earlier sources gave +25% and ~+30%; those look like different vintages or different measures (system quota versus company ambition). The 30-35% figure is the one two sources now agree on. actuals._guidance_CORRECTED_2026_07_28: Was [39400, 39500], which was wrong at the top. MBB's plan is +15-20% on 2025, and the source gives both ends explicitly: 39,400 to 41,121. The 39,500 understated the ceiling by ~1,621bn. Cross-check: 39,400/1.15 implies FY2025 PBT of 34,261, and 34,261 x 1.20 = 41,113, within rounding of 41,121. WHAT THE CORRECTION CHANGES. This morning's inversion said base sits just below guidance and bull just above. On the corrected range the picture is cleaner and different: bear 35,000 and base 38,125 are BOTH BELOW the bottom of guidance, and bull 41,250 is only just above the top. Add the street's FY26 projection of 42,756, which is ABOVE our bull. SO OUR MBB BRANCHES SIT AT OR BELOW EVERY EXTERNAL ESTIMATE - the company's own floor, its ceiling, and the street. That is not necessarily wrong; conservatism is a defensible choice. But it should be a CHOSEN conservatism, and these branches were typed in with nothing deriving them (_NO_DRIVER_MODEL_2026_07_28). It cuts in an interesting direction: the optimizer wants MBB as its joint-largest add while modelling its earnings more conservatively than anyone else does, which if anything strengthens rather than weakens the case.
actuals._credit_ytd_status: PERIOD AMBIGUOUS - corrected 2026-07-29 10:53. Recorded yesterday as '~10% YTD at Q2'. The source article is dated 30-Jun and its HEADLINE reads 'credit continues to accelerate to 10% in Q2', but its BODY says 'cho den thang 5' - as of MAY. Those are different periods and the article does not resolve which it means. WHY IT MATTERS: if 10% is an END-MAY figure, June adds more and H1 credit growth is ABOVE 10%. The H2 requirement computed yesterday - +18.2% to +22.7% to reach a 30-35% full-year target - is then TOO DEMANDING, and MBB's position is better than that entry implied. If it is an end-June figure, yesterday's arithmetic stands. STILL AN ESTIMATE EITHER WAY (T4/T5), not a filed figure, and the H1 statement settles both the level and the period in one line. The field is left at 0.10 and relabelled rather than adjusted, because guessing June from May would invent a number.
actuals._THE_ESTIMATE_SOURCE_JUST_MISSED_BADLY_2: EVIDENCE-QUALITY FINDING on the number this watch list uses as MBB's reference. The 8,812bn Q2 PBT estimate is VCBS's, at +18% YoY. VCBS also forecast ACB's Q2 PBT at 6,703bn, ALSO +18% YoY. ACB then filed: PBT FELL about 12% on sharply higher provisions, while net interest income rose 16.5% (logged 27-Jul). That is a THIRTY PERCENTAGE POINT miss, in the optimistic direction, by the same house on the same metric in the same quarter. NOTE THE SHARED +18%. Both forecasts assume the same growth rate for two different banks, which looks more like a house assumption than two independent analyses. WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN: that MBB will miss. ACB and MBB are different books. WHAT IT DOES MEAN: calibration forecast #4 is effectively a bet on VCBS being right, and the +/-10% band set at 03:53 today (6,347-7,757bn NPAT) assumes broker dispersion of about 10%. An ACB-sized miss would put MBB near 4,935bn NPAT, far outside that band. The band is NOT being widened - moving it now, after seeing evidence pointing one way, is exactly the post-hoc adjustment pre-registration exists to prevent. It stays at +/-10% and the miss gets recorded honestly if it happens. THE MECHANISM TO WATCH is PROVISIONS, not revenue. ACB's miss was entirely below the revenue line - income grew, profit fell. If a sector provisioning cycle is under way, MBB's own NPL target of 'no more than 1.5%' and its credit cost are where it would show. The pre-registered H2 table built on 28-Jul does not depend on the VCBS estimate at all, which is why it is the more useful artifact.
actuals._CREDIT_TRAJECTORY_ANCHORED_2026_07_29: Q1/2026 CREDIT PINNED, and it settles the period question by arithmetic rather than by reading a headline more carefully. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES this sweep give MBB Q1/2026 credit outstanding of OVER 1.14 MILLION TY (1,140,000bn), UP 3.3% ON END-2025, with deposits ~1.07 million ty and NPL 1.42%. Tier T5, press reporting a filed Q1 statement. WHY THIS RESOLVES _credit_ytd_status. That note flagged that the '10%' figure could be end-May YTD or a Q2 quarterly increment, and said the difference mattered. It cannot be a quarterly increment: Q1 YTD was 3.3%, so a further +10% IN the quarter would put YTD at ~13.3%, which contradicts the same source's body text saying 10% YTD as of May. THE 10% IS CUMULATIVE YTD AT END-MAY. So the profile is +3.3% through March and +6.7pp across April and May alone - credit is ACCELERATING SHARPLY, not tracking flat, and end-June H1 is likely ABOVE 10%. WHICH CUTS AGAINST THE NOTE ON FILE. The recorded read was 'H2 must add +18.2% to +22.7%, the same shape as VPB's problem'. On this trajectory the H1 base is higher and the H2 requirement is correspondingly lower, so MBB's version of that problem is MILDER than VPB's, not the same shape. NOT OVERWRITING credit_growth_ytd_q2_est - the H1 statement is due 30 July under Circular 96/2020 and settles level and period together, tomorrow. CONFIDENCE HELD AT 0.55. This is press about a Q1 filing, tier T5, and charter s2 permits confidence to rise only on T1-T2 primary documents. The filing lands tomorrow.
actuals._Q1_DETAIL_ADDED_2026_07_29: Q1/2026 consolidated NPAT 7,703bn (+15.4%), of which 7,516bn to parent shareholders. T5 press on the filed Q1 statement. TWO CHECKS PASS: 9,628 PBT x 0.80 = 7,702.4 against the stated 7,703, so the effective tax rate is exactly 20% and the PBT and NPAT on file describe the same entity; and parent share is 7,516 / 7,703 = 97.6%, so minority interests are ~2.4% and consolidated-vs-parent is NOT a live ambiguity for MBB the way it is for KDH.

NOTE WHAT THIS CORRECTS in _guidance_CORRECTED_2026_07_28, which concluded 'OUR MBB BRANCHES SIT AT OR BELOW EVERY EXTERNAL ESTIMATE'. That was true of the estimates then on file. actuals._Q1_PBT_DISCREPANCY_RESOLVED_2026_07_30: THE 9,500 vs 9,628 GAP FLAGGED ON 29-JUL IS A STATUS DIFFERENCE, NOT AN ERROR. At MB's AGM on 18-Apr-2026 the CEO gave group consolidated Q1 PBT as 9,500bn (+13.3%) and PARENT BANK ALONE as 8,866bn (+15.3%). The 9,628bn (+14.8%) in this file is the FILED consolidated statement. So 9,500 was a PRELIMINARY figure quoted at an April meeting and 9,628 is the final - charter s3's fifth check, filed actual versus guidance versus estimate, and the file already holds the right one. NEW AND USEFUL: the parent/consolidated split. Parent 8,866 against consolidated 9,628 means the SUBSIDIARIES CONTRIBUTE ~762bn, about 8% OF GROUP PBT. That sizes the non-bank ring - MBS, MB Ageas, MBV and the rest - and it is worth having before the H1 print, because it bounds how much of any beat or miss can come from outside the bank. It also means consolidated-versus-parent is a real distinction for MBB even though minority interests are only ~2.4% of NPAT.
actuals._PROVISIONING_NUMBER_UNDERCUTS_MY_OWN_RE: I NOW HAVE THE NUMBER, AND IT DOES NOT SUPPORT WHAT I WROTE THIS MORNING. MBB's Q1/2026 credit-risk provisioning was 3,455bn, UP 15.7% YoY, with NPL at 1.42%. WHAT I CLAIMED AT 09:53. I strengthened the pre-registered read on calibration forecast #4 from 'peers suggest' to 'MBB was already doing this', on the basis of press describing MBB's Q1 as having 'a sharp increase in risk provisioning' (tang manh trich lap du phong rui ro). I took a QUALITATIVE CHARACTERISATION as quantitative evidence. WHAT THE NUMBER SAYS. Provisions +15.7% against Q1 PBT +14.8% - provisioning grew essentially IN LINE with the business, not disproportionately to it. That is not the ACB pattern at all. ACB's Q2 had NET INTEREST INCOME +16.5% AND PROFIT -12%, which is provisions overwhelming a growing top line. MBB's Q1 shows nothing of the kind. SO THE STRENGTHENING IS WITHDRAWN. The ORIGINAL read registered 29-Jul 19:53 STANDS on its own footing - it rests on ACB and VIB actually printing -12% and -8% on provisions, which is unchanged. What does not stand is this morning's claim that MBB itself was already showing the pattern in Q1. It was not. RECORDED BEFORE MBB FILES, WHICH IS THE ONLY TIME THIS IS WORTH ANYTHING. Withdrawing a strengthening after the print would be indistinguishable from retrofitting. MBB is still unfiled at 20:54 on its deadline day. THIRD SELF-CORRECTION TODAY AND THE SAME SPECIES AS THE OTHER TWO: treating a qualitative phrase ('sharp increase', 'declining revenue') as if it carried a number. The fix is the same each time - get the figure before building on the adjective. FOR CONTEXT WHEN THE PRINT LANDS: provisions were 36% of Q1 pre-tax profit, and NPL 1.42%.
actuals._Q2_DID_NOT_APPEAR_ON_DEADLINE_DAY_2026_: MBB'S Q2/2026 DID NOT SURFACE ON 30 JULY, ITS CIRCULAR 96/2020 DEADLINE DAY. Recorded because a DATED CATALYST FAILED TO LAND ON ITS DATE, which is charter s1 test 3, and because calibration forecast #4 was due to resolve today and did not. WHAT I CAN AND CANNOT SAY. I checked across SIXTEEN CONSECUTIVE HOURLY SWEEPS spanning the whole Vietnamese day - pre-market, both sessions, post-close and the full evening - and no Q2 or H1 figure appeared in any Vietnamese or English source. THAT IS ABSENCE IN PRESS SEARCH, NOT ABSENCE ON THE EXCHANGE. Both the HOSE and MB investor-relations disclosure pages return proxy 403 from this environment, so the filing channel itself cannot be read. I AM NOT CALLING A DISCLOSURE BREACH, because I cannot verify one. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE INFORMATIVE PART. KDH filed the same day and press had detailed figures - revenue, profit, inventory, cash flow, borrowings - within hours. Several unrelated names (DCM, VRE, NTL, AGG, BCE, HDC) were covered in same-day round-ups. MBB produced nothing across the entire day. A filing that had occurred would ordinarily have been picked up; that it was not is evidence, though it is not proof. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND HOUSEKEEPING. MBB is 6.5% of the book and the engine's JOINT-LARGEST PROPOSED ADD at +5.5pp to 12.0%. It is also the one bank with NO DRIVER MODEL, so its branches are typed in rather than derived. A name that is simultaneously the biggest proposed purchase, the least modelled, and now the slowest to disclose is worth a human looking at directly. NOTHING CHANGED. No branch, probability, weight or confidence. Absence of a filing is not evidence about earnings, and treating it as such would be exactly the inference-from-silence this file has avoided all week. Forecast #4 remains OPEN and unresolved.
actuals._Q2_FILED_2026_07_31: MBB FILED. Q2/2026 PBT 10,560bn, UP MORE THAN 40%; Q2 NPAT attributable to parent 8,229.06bn (+40.01%); H1 NPAT-to-parent 15,744.58bn (+26.51%). Q2 net interest income 16,893.65bn (+36.55%), Q2 total operating income 20,434.31bn (+18.49%). Balance sheet at 30-Jun: total credit 1.26 MILLION TY, of which CUSTOMER LOANS +13.2% YTD to over 1.22 million ty; total assets +7.3% to over 1.73 million ty; NPL 1.45% (up from 1.42% at Q1); NPL COVERAGE 93.63% (up from 92.24% at Q1). Tier T5 - press reporting the filed statement, not the statement. THREE ARITHMETIC CHECKS RUN BEFORE LOGGING, ALL PASS. (1) Q1 parent 7,515.52 + Q2 parent 8,229.06 = 15,744.58, EXACTLY the stated H1 - so 8,229.06 is Q2 NPAT-to-parent on a consolidated basis, the same measure as the 7,516 already on file, and it is a genuine Q2 figure rather than a cumulative one. (2) Q2 PBT 10,560 x 0.80 = 8,448 consolidated NPAT; 8,229.06 / 8,448 = 97.4% to parent, against 97.6% in Q1 - the minority-interest share is stable, so PBT and NPAT here describe the same entity. (3) H1 PBT = 9,628 + 10,560 = 20,188. This is charter s3's measure and entity check done BEFORE the number went in the file, which is the discipline that failed on KDH twelve hours earlier.
actuals._TWO_FIGURES_IN_THE_SAME_COVERAGE_WERE_S: PERIOD CHECK CAUGHT TWO Q1 FIGURES BEING CARRIED IN Q2-CONTEXT COVERAGE, AND THEY WERE NOT LOGGED. A search return offered, alongside the genuine Q2 figures, 'provisioning 3,455bn (+15.7%)' and 'customer loans 1.12 million ty (+3.3%)'. BOTH ARE THE Q1 NUMBERS ALREADY IN THIS FILE - q1_provisions is 3,455 and q1_provisions_yoy is 0.157; q1_credit_growth_ytd is 0.033. A confirming search returned the provisioning line explicitly attached to Q1/2026 ('MB trich lap du phong rui ro tin dung 3.454,8 ty dong, tang 15,7%' with NPL 1.42% at end-Q1), and the true Q2 loan figure is 1.22 million ty at +13.2% YTD, not 1.12 at +3.3%. SO H1 PROVISIONING IS STILL UNKNOWN and no provisioning number has been recorded for Q2. That matters more than usual: provisioning is the exact mechanism the pre-registered read named, and the temptation was to log a number that would have made the read look testable. WHAT SAVED IT was noticing that the candidate figure was IDENTICAL to one already on file. That is the eighth period/entity trap this week and the same species as the 26-Jul near-miss that put the six checks in charter s3 in the first place. The tell generalises: A NEW FIGURE THAT EXACTLY EQUALS AN OLD ONE IS USUALLY THE OLD ONE. NPL 1.45% and coverage 93.63% survived the same check - both are stated as CHANGES from the Q1 values, which is what a genuine new-period figure looks like.
actuals._PRE_REGISTERED_H2_TABLE_FIRES_AND_SAYS_: THE 28-JUL PRE-REGISTERED READ RESOLVES, AND IT RESOLVES AGAINST THE BRANCHES. That table was written before the print and mapped each H1 outcome to the H2 growth every fy26e_npat branch would then require. ACTUAL H1 PBT IS 20,188bn, which lands in the row the pre-registration singled out: 'at H1 of 20,000 or above, even the BULL branch needs almost no further growth, which would mean the branches have stopped discriminating and need rebuilding rather than celebrating.' COMPUTED ON THE ACTUAL: bear (FY PBT 35,000) needs H2 -26.6% versus H1; base (38,125) needs H2 -11.2%; bull (41,250) needs H2 +4.3%. VIETNAMESE BANK PROFIT IS SECOND-HALF WEIGHTED, so a flat H2 is the conservative case, and a flat H2 gives FY26 PBT of 40,376 - ABOVE base and just below bull. TWO OF THREE BRANCHES NOW REQUIRE PROFIT TO FALL OUTRIGHT. SO fy26e_npat 28,000/30,500/33,000 IS CONTRADICTED FROM BELOW. This is the OPPOSITE SIGN of the KDH problem and it corrects something I was about to write: the branches are NOT 'supported' by H1, they are exceeded on trajectory. A flat-H2 FY of 40,376 sits inside company guidance [39,400, 41,121] and near MAS's 40,726, so the conservatism noted in _guidance_CORRECTED_2026_07_28 is now not merely conservative but likely wrong. NOT REBUILT HERE. Re-deriving fy26e_npat is a human-only edit under charter s4 and the pre-registration's own instruction is to rebuild, which is more than an automated run may do. ESCALATED.
actuals._CONFIDENCE_HELD_AT_0_55_AND_WHY_THAT_IS: CONFIDENCE UNCHANGED AT 0.55, for the charter's reason, not for KDH's reason. CHARTER s2 IS EXPLICIT: 'Confidence rises only on T1-T2 primary documents. Press coverage ABOUT a filing is not the filing.' What this sweep has is T5 press reporting a filed statement. The same rule was applied to hold confidence on 29-Jul when the Q1 detail landed the same way, and applying it in one direction but not the other would make it decorative. The HOSE and MB IR disclosure pages still return proxy 403 from this environment, so the primary document cannot be reached from here - this is OPEN-DECISIONS item 17 binding again. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE KDH CASE, because the two look similar and are not. On KDH, raising confidence would have AMPLIFIED BRANCHES THE PRINT HAD JUST CONTRADICTED FROM ABOVE, flattering a bad quarter; confidence was held as a deliberate deviation. On MBB the branches are contradicted FROM BELOW, so raising confidence would amplify branches that understate a good quarter - it would move E[r] up toward a number that is still too low. The defect is the same one-scalar-two-meanings problem in both, but here the charter already forbids the move, so no deviation is needed. THE FIX IN BOTH CASES IS THE SAME AND IS HUMAN-ONLY: re-derive the branches. Confidence is not a substitute for that in either direction.
actuals._CREDIT_YTD_RESOLVED_2026_07_31: credit_growth_ytd_q2_est (0.10) AND _credit_ytd_status ARE NOW SETTLED BY THE FILING. Actual H1 customer-loan growth is +13.2% YTD, and the profile reads +3.3% at end-March, ~10% at end-May, +13.2% at end-June. THAT CONFIRMS THE END-MAY READING the 29-Jul note argued for on arithmetic grounds and rules out the Q2-increment reading, which would have implied ~13.3% YTD in March-to-June alone. The estimate on file was low by 3.2pp because it was a May figure being read as a June one. WHAT IT DOES TO THE H2 REQUIREMENT: reaching the 30-35% full-year target now needs H2 credit growth of +14.8% to +19.3%, against the +18.2% to +22.7% recorded on 28-Jul off the 10% base. MILDER THAN RECORDED, and milder than VPB's version of the same problem, which is the direction the 29-Jul note predicted. Note the two loan measures are not the same thing: TOTAL CREDIT is 1.26 million ty and CUSTOMER LOANS are 1.22 million ty, the gap being corporate bonds and other credit exposure. The +13.2% is the customer-loan figure. The 25%-versus-30-35% target question in _target_conflict is NOT resolved by this - a half-year outturn does not tell you which target was approved.
actuals._THE_RATIO_IS_FLATTERED_BY_LOAN_GROWTH_2: THE ASSET-QUALITY NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE RATIO. Group 3-5 bad debt rose 27% TO NEARLY 17,800bn. The NPL RATIO went 1.42% -> 1.45%, which reads as almost nothing. IT READS AS ALMOST NOTHING BECAUSE THE DENOMINATOR GREW 13.2% YTD. A 27% rise in the numerator against a 13.2% rise in the denominator produces a 3bp move in the ratio, and the 3bp is what the coverage reported. CROSS-CHECK PASSES: 1,220,000bn of customer loans x 1.45% = 17,690bn against the stated 'nearly 17,800'. RECORDED AS A NEAR-MATCH, NOT A MATCH - 'gan 17.800' is a rounded phrase and 17,690 is a derived figure, so they agree in magnitude and are not the same number. PERIOD OF THE 27% IS NOT STATED AND IS NOT ASSUMED. If YTD, end-2025 bad debt was ~14,016bn on loans of ~1,077,700bn, an NPL ratio of ~1.30% - so the honest description of the half is 1.30% -> 1.45%, not 1.42% -> 1.45%. If YoY the picture differs. The YTD reading is the more plausible because every other comparison in the same coverage is against end-Q1 or end-2025, but it is NOT ESTABLISHED and is flagged rather than asserted. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO THE SCORED READ. Calibration forecast #4's pre-registered read said MBB would MISS ON CREDIT COST. It was scored WRONG on 31-Jul because MBB BEAT OUTRIGHT, which was the explicitly stipulated falsifier. THAT SCORE STANDS AND IS NOT REVISITED. Finding credit deterioration in the balance sheet AFTER scoring does not partially rescue a read that was wrong about the outcome - that is precisely the retrofitting the pre-registration existed to prevent, and the temptation to do it is the reason this paragraph is here. WHAT IT DOES ADD, SEPARATELY: coverage ROSE from 92.24% to 93.63% while bad debt rose 27%, so RESERVES GREW FASTER THAN NPLs - roughly 29% - to a stock of about 16,666bn. MBB PROVISIONED SUBSTANTIALLY AND STILL GREW PBT 40%. That is the closest this file has got to the missing H1 provisioning charge after four attempts, and it is a BOUND ON THE BALANCE, NOT THE P&L FIGURE: reserve stock change equals provisioning charge minus write-offs, and write-offs are unknown. THE H1 PROVISIONING EXPENSE REMAINS UNFOUND.
actuals._A_NINTH_PERIOD_TRAP_CAUGHT_BY_THE_CIR_2: 'CHI PHI HOAT DONG TRONG KY DAT 5.627 TY DONG' - operating expenses in the period - APPEARED IN AN ARTICLE HEADLINED ABOUT THE HALF YEAR, WHERE IT READS AS AN H1 FIGURE. IT IS Q2. THE ARITHMETIC THAT CAUGHT IT: the same coverage states H1 CIR of 26.24% on H1 total operating income of 37,865bn, which implies H1 OPEX OF 9,936bn. At 5,627 the implied CIR would be 14.9%, contradicting the stated 26.24% in the same article. Read as Q2 it reconciles: q1_opex 4,347 already on file, plus 5,627, gives H1 opex 9,974 and a CIR of 26.34% - within rounding of the stated 26.24%. TWO MORE RECONCILIATIONS PASS IN THE SAME PASS. H1 TOI: q1_toi 17,430 + q2_toi 20,434.31 = 37,864.31 against the stated 37,865 - EXACT, which independently confirms the Q2 TOI figure logged yesterday. And the H1 PBT of 20,188bn, which THIS FILE COMPUTED yesterday as 9,628 + 10,560, is now STATED DIRECTLY by a headline ('lai hon 20.188 ty dong sau 6 thang, tang hon 27%'). A derived figure has become a reported one and they agree exactly. THE SEQUENTIAL PICTURE IS WORSE THAN THE ANNUAL ONE, AND BOTH ARE TRUE. H1 CIR 26.24% consolidated and 24.17% at the parent are an IMPROVEMENT of 2-2.7pp on 2025 - that is what the coverage leads with. BUT Q2 CIR IS 27.54% AGAINST Q1'S 24.94%, WORSE BY 2.60pp QUARTER ON QUARTER. Cost efficiency improved year-on-year and deteriorated sequentially, and a reader given only the first number would not know the second. Same shape as the VCI lesson from 26-Jul: '+36% YoY' and '-26% QoQ' described one quarter and every source reported the first.

actuals._THE_CASH_DIVIDEND_AND_THE_RIGHTS_ISSUE_: AN ARITHMETIC IDENTITY THIS FILE HELD ALL THE PIECES OF AND NEVER DIVIDED. MBB's 15% stock dividend is 12,082bn, WHICH IMPLIES CHARTER CAPITAL OF 80,547bn. Ten percent of that is 8,055bn - EXACTLY the cash dividend paid from 17-JUL. And the rights issue of 805.5m shares at par 10,000 RAISES 8,055bn, THE SAME NUMBER AGAIN. All three figures were already in this file separately; none had been divided into the others. SO THE CASH GOING OUT AND THE CASH COMING BACK IN ARE IDENTICAL. Both are 10% of charter capital at par. FOR A HOLDER WHO TAKES UP RIGHTS IN FULL, THE NET CASH FLOW ACROSS THE TWO EVENTS IS ZERO - and after the 5% PIT on the cash dividend it is slightly NEGATIVE, about -403bn across the register, because the dividend is taxed and the subscription is not discounted for that. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a claim that the package is economically neutral. IT IS NOT. The rights are priced at 10,000 against a market price of 22,050 - 45.4% of market, a 54.6% DISCOUNT - so the round trip converts taxed cash into shares at well under half price. The correct reading is that MBB's headline '25% distribution' is, for a participating holder, LARGELY A ROUND TRIP IN CASH TERMS whose value sits in the subscription discount rather than in the distribution. A holder who does NOT take up gets the cash, pays the tax, and is diluted at 10,000. AND ONE RECORD DATE COVERS BOTH. Press states the final registration date for exercising rights under BOTH plans - the 15% stock dividend and the 805.5m-share offering - falls at the SAME time point, per the legal requirement. So this is ONE dated catalyst, not two, and when it lands it lands together. A DATE WAS OFFERED AND IS NOT LOGGED. A search summary attached '14 August' to this, but described it as the record date for '2024 DIVIDENDS' - a YEAR that does not match, and the summary itself hedged with 'appears to be'. That is the tenth instance this week of a plausible date attached to the wrong period, and it is exactly the shape of the MBB 10-Jun/10-Jul error already on file. NO RECORD DATE IS RECORDED. The 15% and the rights remain undated pending a disclosure that states the year.
actuals._CAP_NOW_CROSS_CHECK_2026_08_02_1153: CAP_NOW MAY BE 17.9% TOO HIGH, AND THE DIRECTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Implied shares 9,495m against a pre-dividend charter of 80,550bn (8,055m). On the pre-dividend count mu_raw goes +16.0% -> +36.7% (+20.7pp, trigger 3); on a post-15%-dividend count of 9,263m, cap_now is only +2.5% off and the delta is +2.9pp (no trigger). WHICH IS TRUE DEPENDS ON THE EX-DATE AND ON WHETHER THE 22,050 PRICE IS ADJUSTED - neither established, so NEITHER IS ASSUMED. IF the larger reading holds it bears directly on OPEN-DECISIONS item 19, which records that MBB's expected return did not move at all on a +40% quarter and stayed at +8.8%: 16.0% x 0.55 confidence = 8.8% exactly, and on the corrected cap it would be 36.7% x 0.55 = +20.2%. THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING, and it must not be used to argue for the add until the ex-date is settled. Not retuned.
actuals._PROVISIONING_IS_FLATTERING_REPORTED_PBT: See tcb.model._PROVISIONING_IS_FLATTERING_REPORTED_PBT_AND_THE_PIPELINE_IS_GROWING_2026_08_02_2053 for the full cross-bank analysis. MBB SPECIFICS: H1/2026 provisions 7,701.9bn, DOWN 0.9% and effectively FLAT while PPOP grew 17.9%. Provisions/PPOP 32.9% -> 27.6%. 9.2pp of the 27.1% PBT growth is lower provisioning intensity, not operations. actuals._THE_GAP_FOUND_ON_THE_THIRD_ATTEMPT_WAS_:
WENT AFTER A NAMED GAP - the 03-Aug note reads 'STILL UNKNOWN AND STILL THE GAP: MBB'S H1 PROVISIONING FIGURE. A second search this sweep again returned only the Q1 number.' THIRD ATTEMPT, DIFFERENT ANGLE, AND IT RETURNED.

H1/2026 CREDIT PROVISIONING COST IS 7,702bn, DOWN 0.9% YEAR ON YEAR, against PBT of 20,188bn, +27.1%.

AND THE FIRST THING TO SAY IS THAT THIS FILE ALREADY HAD IT. Open item 26 reads: 'the method is cheap and validated: PPOP = PBT + provisions, and provisions derive as TOI - opex - PBT (MBB: DERIVED 7,703 VS REPORTED 7,701.9)'. SO A REPORTED H1 FIGURE WAS SITTING INSIDE ITEM 26 WHILE A PROSE NOTE ELSEWHERE CALLED IT UNKNOWN AND SENT TWO SWEEPS LOOKING FOR IT. TODAY'S 7,702 CONFIRMS BOTH TO WITHIN 0.01%, AND THE INTENSITY RECONCILES EXACTLY: 7,702 / (20,188 + 7,702) = 27.62%, AGAINST ITEM 26'S STATED 27.6%. THIRD FIELD-VERSUS-PROSE CONTRADICTION FOUND IN THIS FILE IN TWENTY-FOUR HOURS, after KDH's Bình Trưng Mới date and effective_broker_pct. THE COST HERE WAS THREE SEARCHES FOR A NUMBER ALREADY HELD.

NOW THE PART THAT IS GENUINELY NEW, AND IT RUNS AGAINST ITEM 26'S OWN CHARACTERISATION OF THIS NAME. Q1/2026 PROVISIONS WERE 3,454.8bn (+15.7% YoY, already on file), SO Q2/2026 PROVISIONS ARE 7,702 - 3,454.8 = 4,247.2bn. THAT IS UP 22.9% ON Q1. AND PROVISIONING INTENSITY OF PPOP ROSE WITHIN THE HALF: Q1 26.41%, Q2 28.68%. ITEM 26 DESCRIBES MBB AS 'PBT +27.1% on PPOP +17.9%, PROVISIONS FLAT while the NPL balance rose 27% - 9.2pp is provisioning'. 'FLAT' IS TRUE OF THE HALF-YEAR AGGREGATE AND CONCEALS A RISING QUARTERLY PATH. MBB IS PROVISIONING MORE IN Q2 THAN IN Q1, BOTH ABSOLUTELY AND AS A SHARE OF PPOP, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM FLATTERED.

THE YEAR-ON-YEAR FALL IS A BASE EFFECT AND IT IS WORTH SHOWING RATHER THAN ASSERTING. Deriving the 2025 split from the stated growth rates: H1/2025 provisions 7,771.9bn, Q1/2025 2,986.0bn, SO Q2/2025 WAS 4,785.9bn. AGAINST THAT, Q2/2026's 4,247.2bn IS DOWN 11.3% - a fall against a heavy prior quarter, not a reduction against the run-rate. STATED WITH ITS WEAKNESS: THE 2025 QUARTERLY SPLIT IS DERIVED FROM TWO PERCENTAGES, NOT REPORTED, so the -11.3% is a construction and the +22.9% quarter-on-quarter figure - built from two reported 2026 numbers - is the sounder of the two.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO ITEM 26. IT DOES NOT OVERTURN THE SECTOR FINDING: system LLR coverage fell to 79.78% while system NPLs rose 48tn in H1, and that stands. IT DOES SOFTEN THE MBB LEG SPECIFICALLY, AND ITEM 26 ALREADY POINTED THAT WAY - it recorded that 'the cross-section discriminates: MBB's NPL 1.45% and coverage 93.63% RISING both beat the sector, consistent with its branches being the defensible ones', and that MBB needs only 1.08x its prior-year intensity to justify its base branch against TCB's 2.17x and VPB's 1.25x. TODAY ADDS A QUARTERLY PATH POINTING THE SAME WAY. THREE INDEPENDENT SIGNS NOW AGREE THAT MBB IS THE LEAST FLATTERED OF THE THREE BANKS. NOTHING IS RETUNED - branch construction is human-only under charter s4.

AND A MEASURE TRAP APPEARING AT A SECOND BANK. Today's coverage puts MBB's CREDIT at 1,256,000bn, +13.2%. This file holds 1,220,000bn of CUSTOMER LOANS, also +13.2% YTD - A GAP OF 36,000bn ON THE SAME GROWTH RATE. THAT IS THE CREDIT-VERSUS-CUSTOMER-LOANS DISTINCTION THE FILE IDENTIFIED AT TCB, WHERE THE DIFFERENCE WAS NAMED AS INFRASTRUCTURE AND SOCIAL-HOUSING LENDING EXCLUDED FROM CREDIT LIMITS. THE SAME TWO MEASURES ARE NOW VISIBLE AT MBB AND THE FILE HAS BEEN CARRYING ONE OF THEM. WHETHER MBB'S 36,000bn GAP HAS THE SAME COMPOSITION IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT ASSUMED - the credit_quota_exemptions entry already warned that cross-bank credit-growth comparisons are not like-for-like, and this is a second instance of exactly that.

NOTHING MODELLED. No branch, probability, price, weight or confidence moved.
actuals._MIC_IS_SIZED_AND_THE_INSURANCE_PILLAR_I:
CLOSES THE GAP LEFT OPEN AT 01:53 - 'MIC'S PROFIT IS NOT GIVEN, ONLY REVENUE, SO THE LARGER OF MBB'S TWO INSURERS REMAINS UNSIZED ON THE MEASURE THAT MATTERS'.

MIC (MIG, listed on HOSE). FY2026 TARGETS: PREMIUM REVENUE ABOUT 7,038bn, UP 30%; PROFIT ABOUT 550bn, UP 34.5%. Aiming for TOP 3 non-life market share. H1/2026 revenue of 3,750bn on file is 53.3% of that premium target. MB'S STAKE: TWO FIGURES CAME BACK, 69.58% OF CHARTER CAPITAL AND 68.37% OF SHARES, NEITHER DATED, DIFFERING BY 1.21 POINTS.

AND HERE IS WHY I USE THEM ANYWAY, HAVING REFUSED AN UNDATED PERCENTAGE ON THIS EXACT SUBJECT AT 01:53. THE REFUSAL THEN WAS RIGHT BECAUSE THE QUESTION WAS A LOOK-THROUGH WEIGHT, WHICH IS SENSITIVE TO THE PERCENTAGE. THE QUESTION HERE IS WHETHER THE INSURANCE ARM IS MATERIAL TO GROUP PROFIT, AND THE ANSWER IS THE SAME AT BOTH ENDS OF THE RANGE: 550bn x 68.37% = 376.0bn AND x 69.58% = 382.7bn - AGAINST MBB'S ANNUALISED PBT OF ABOUT 40,376bn THAT IS 0.93% TO 0.95%, OR 1.19% TO 1.22% AGAINST ANNUALISED NPAT-TO-PARENT OF ABOUT 31,489bn. A 1.21-POINT SPREAD IN THE STAKE MOVES THE ANSWER BY 0.02 OF A PERCENTAGE POINT. AN IMPRECISE INPUT IS USABLE WHEN THE CONCLUSION IS INSENSITIVE TO ITS RANGE, AND THAT CONDITION IS TESTABLE RATHER THAN A MATTER OF JUDGMENT.

SO THE THIRD LEG OF THE INSURANCE STORY LANDS WHERE THE SECOND DID. At 16:53 on 05-Aug I called this 'a whole earnings pillar'. At 01:53 I corrected that using MB Life alone - PBT 270bn = 1.34% of H1 PBT before the JV split. MIC, THE LARGER ARM BY REVENUE, IS ABOUT 1% OF GROUP PROFIT ON ITS OWN FY TARGET. AN ABSOLUTE UPPER BOUND, ASSUMING MB OWNED 100% OF BOTH AND BOTH HIT PLAN: (550 + 540) / 40,376 = 2.7% OF PBT. THE TRUE FIGURE IS BELOW THAT ON BOTH COUNTS - MB owns neither outright and MB Life's stake is still unestablished. THE PILLAR LANGUAGE IS NOW WRONG ON BOTH ARMS RATHER THAN ONE, AND THE CORRECTION IS COMPLETE.

TWO MEASURE CAVEATS KEPT. (a) MIC'S 550bn IS A TARGET, NOT AN ACTUAL. (b) WHETHER IT IS PRE- OR POST-TAX IS NOT STATED, WHICH IS WHY BOTH THE PBT AND THE NPAT PAIRINGS ARE SHOWN RATHER THAN ONE. Neither caveat changes the order of magnitude.

AND ONE FORWARD ITEM WORTH LOGGING. MIC'S 2026 AGM, HELD 09-APRIL, APPROVED A STRATEGY OF FINDING A STRATEGIC PARTNER. FOR A SUBSIDIARY 68-70% OWNED BY A HOLDING IN THIS BOOK, 'STRATEGIC PARTNER' USUALLY MEANS A STAKE SALE OR A PRIMARY ISSUE THAT DILUTES THE PARENT. NOTHING IS ANNOUNCED AND NO SIZE IS KNOWN. Recorded as a watch item, not as an event - and it is small: a partial sale of a stake worth roughly 1% of group profit cannot move this book.

WHAT IT DOES TO THE QUESTION LIST FOR MBB'S MANAGEMENT. The question 'what percentage of MB Life and MIC does MB own' is now HALF ANSWERED - MIC is 68-70% and the number barely matters. THE REMAINING HALF IS MB LIFE, AND THE BETTER VERSION OF THE QUESTION IS NOW NARROWER: NOT THE STAKE, BUT WHETHER EITHER ARM IS EXPECTED TO REACH A SCALE THAT CHANGES THE GROUP - because at roughly 1% each, neither currently does.

NOTHING MODELLED. No branch, probability, price, weight or confidence moved.
actuals._THE_MBV_CRITERION_CANNOT_FIRE_AND_MANAG:
WENT AFTER THE ONE ARMED CRITERION ON THIS NAME THAT NOBODY CAN EVALUATE - 'TRANSFEREE DRAG > 5% OF PBT IN ANY QUARTER'. IT CANNOT FIRE, AND THE REASON IS NOT A DATA GAP.

MBV HAS MOVED FROM CONSECUTIVE LOSSES TO PROFIT SINCE 2025, and MB's chairman states the transferred bank 'will certainly stop making losses this year'. MB has seconded ABOUT 200 STAFF into MBV and seated people on its board, supervisory board and executive committee. A CRITERION THAT MEASURES A P&L DRAG CANNOT EXCEED 5% OF PBT WHEN THE ENTITY BEING MEASURED IS PROFITABLE. FIFTH DEFECTIVE ARMED CRITERION FOUND THIS WEEK, AND IT IS THE SECOND OF THE 'MECHANISM OVERTAKEN BY FACTS' TYPE after VPX's five-licence cap - the other three (TCB's Masterise boundary, VPX's gross-versus-net FVTPL, KDH's consolidation basis) were undefined SUBJECTS.

AND THE CRITERION MEASURES THE WRONG QUANTITY, WHICH IS THE SHARPER POINT. THIS FILE'S OWN FRAMING OF THE MBV COST IS 'ROE EROSION 25.0% -> 20.9% AS THE PRICE OF THE TRANSFER, WHICH BOUGHT A 30-35% CREDIT ALLOWANCE'. THAT IS A CAPITAL STORY, NOT A P&L ONE. THE COST OF ABSORBING A WEAK BANK SHOWS UP AS CAPITAL DEPLOYED AT A LOW RETURN AND AS DILUTED GROUP ROE - NOT AS A LOSS LINE THAT CAN BE COMPARED TO PBT. THE CRITERION WATCHES A LINE THAT HAS TURNED POSITIVE WHILE THE ACTUAL COST SITS IN A RATIO IT DOES NOT LOOK AT. Human-only under charter s4; flagged, not rewritten.

WHAT IS NOT DISCLOSED AND IS NOT INFERRED: MBV'S ACCUMULATED LOSSES AND THEIR SPECIFIC EFFECT ON MB'S CONSOLIDATED RESULT. Searched and not found. That half of the question remains one only management can answer.

AND THE SEARCH RETURNED SOMETHING BIGGER THAN WHAT IT WENT FOR. MANAGEMENT'S OWN 2026 PLAN IS PROFIT GROWTH OF 15%, HOPING FOR 20%, AGAINST A CREDIT-GROWTH TARGET OF 30-35%. THE BANK PLANS TO GROW ITS BALANCE SHEET ROUGHLY TWICE AS FAST AS ITS EARNINGS. AND H1 RAN THE OPPOSITE WAY: CREDIT +13.2%, PBT +27.1% - PROFIT GREW 2.05 TIMES AS FAST AS CREDIT. THE PLAN AND THE HALF-YEAR POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.

SO THE PLAN HAS A SHARP H2 DECELERATION BUILT INTO IT, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT. FY2025 PBT 34,261 IMPLIES H1/2025 OF 15,884 AND H2/2025 OF 18,377. AT +15% THE FULL YEAR IS 39,400, SO H2 MUST DELIVER 19,212 - MINUS 4.8% ON H1 AND PLUS 4.5% YEAR ON YEAR. AT +20% IT IS 41,113, SO H2 MUST DELIVER 20,925 - PLUS 3.7% ON H1 AND PLUS 13.9% YEAR ON YEAR. AGAINST H1's +27.1%, MANAGEMENT'S OWN PLAN IMPLIES H2 PROFIT GROWTH OF ONLY +4.5% TO +13.9%. MEANWHILE CREDIT MUST ACCELERATE: FROM +13.2% AT H1 TO A FULL YEAR OF 30-35% REQUIRES ANOTHER +14.8% TO +19.3% IN H2.

AND THAT CONVERGES WITH ITEM 26 FROM A COMPLETELY DIFFERENT DIRECTION, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS. ITEM 26'S INVERSE ARITHMETIC SAYS MBB NEEDS H2 PROVISIONING INTENSITY OF 35.7% TO JUSTIFY ITS BASE BRANCH, AGAINST 27.6% IN H1 AND 32.9% THE PRIOR YEAR - ONLY 1.08 TIMES PRIOR, THE MOST ACHIEVABLE OF THE THREE BANKS. MANAGEMENT'S PLAN INDEPENDENTLY IMPLIES A BIG H2 PROFIT SLOWDOWN ALONGSIDE FASTER CREDIT. TWO ROUTES - ONE FROM THIS FILE'S PROVISIONING MODEL, ONE FROM THE COMPANY'S OWN GUIDANCE - AGREE THAT H2 IS MEANT TO BE MUCH WEAKER THAN H1 AND THAT PROVISIONING IS THE MECHANISM. THAT IS SUPPORT FOR THE BASE BRANCH FROM OUTSIDE THE MODEL.

IT ALSO REPLACES A QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. 'What is MBV dragging per quarter' is the wrong question now - MBV is profitable. THE RIGHT ONE IS ABOUT CAPITAL AND ABOUT THE SPREAD: WHY IS CREDIT PLANNED AT ROUGHLY TWICE THE PROFIT GROWTH RATE, AND WHICH OF NIM, COST OR PROVISIONING ABSORBS THE DIFFERENCE?

NOTHING MODELLED. No branch, probability, price, weight or confidence moved. NO CRITERION IS DECLARED FIRED - a criterion that cannot fire is not the same as one that has been tested and passed, and saying so is the point.

SOURCE CLASS: these are QUESTIONS ASKED BY ANALYSTS, not MBB disclosure. Numbers embedded in a question are ASSERTED BY THE QUESTIONER and rank below T5.
